_doc: DATA_RUNBOOK §167. Exchange HOLIDAYS the backtest bin carried as trading days: on each date NSE's per-day URL re-served the previous session's file (holiday misdirect) and an old full build stored it, so every listed symbol got a bar that copies its previous session. update_sf_data.drop_phantom_sessions() DROPS every bar on these dates from every symbol, every run (idempotent) — never filled, never re-dated; the copied session is already in the bin for all but 5 of the 17,521 dropped bars (3 zero-close stubs on 20191028: KSERASERA, SUJANAUNI, UVSL; DVL/DTIL on 20211105, emitted by the §89 surgery ledger, whose splice guard drops them once the calendar no longer lists the date). Proven per date, from files: NSE's archive serves no bhavcopy for it (old cm..bhav.csv.zip and UDiFF routes both tried); NSE's own PREV_CLOSE on the next session equals the copied session's close for every symbol in both files (the exchange chains straight over the date); the Nifty 50 close series has no bar; the date is on the repo NSE holiday list (fo_spot_nse.json _holidays); BSE's daily archive has no file (bse_last_trade_archive.json missing_days, scanned 2007-01-01..2023-12-03). Measured 2026-09-25 on the live bin (end 2026-09-25): real sessions repeat the previous close on 2-6% of bars, these 93.0-100%. A NEW date is added here only after the same checks; update_sf_data.phantom_session_audit() names candidates (>= 90% repeat) with ::warning:: but never drops an unproven date.

TATAMOTORS.why: Dead rename fragment (TELCO->TATAMOTORS 1996-2003-12-24; the live series is TMPV from 2003-12-26). Weekend/missing-session inserts put these 34 bars on the fragment before §106h/§106i routed them to the live successor; 26 are exact duplicates of TMPV bars, 8 (2004-04-17..2008-02-19) are anchored on the stale 2003 close (≈430 while Tata Motors traded 505-951) and land in TMPV from scripts/bar_inserts.json instead. While present they made the engine resolve TATAMOTORS (quantmac/F&O rosters) to a series that ends in 2003 for 14 days after each session. DATA_RUNBOOK §169.
